name_en: Kenchin jiru — root vegetables and tofu pan-fried then simmered in dashi
summary_ja: こんにゃくや根菜、豆腐をごま油で炒めてから出汁で煮込む鎌倉発祥の汁物。建長寺の精進料理が起源のひとつとされ、僧侶が落とした豆腐を拾い集めて汁に入れた逸話も残っている。
summary_en: A Kamakura-born soup of root vegetables and tofu, pan-fried in sesame oil before simmering in dashi. One account traces it to the shojin cooking of Kenchoji temple, with a story that a monk once gathered spilled tofu into the pot rather than waste it.
source_title: けんちん汁 神奈川県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Gyu nabe — beef, tofu and greens simmered together from the start in seasoned broth
summary_ja: 牛肉や豆腐、春菊などを味噌や醤油だれで最初から煮込む横浜市発祥の鍋料理。開港後に西洋の肉食文化と出会って生まれ、居酒屋の主人が牛鍋屋を開いたのが始まりと伝わる。
summary_en: A Yokohama-born hot pot of beef, tofu and chrysanthemum greens simmered from the start in a soy or miso-based sauce. Born of the port city's encounter with Western meat-eating culture, it is said to trace to a tavern owner who opened one of the first beef-pot restaurants.
source_title: 牛鍋 神奈川県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
